question: Is LOXL2's human height effect its MATRIX (collagen cross-linking) function or its NUCLEAR (H3K4me3 deamination) function?
interpretation: Erasing less H3K4me3 = TALLER; writing less H3K4me3 = SHORTER. Opposite signs, both arms very well powered.

Kdm5b_hom_body_length.note: ERASER loss SHORTER - opposite to the human prediction

impc_verdict: UNINFORMATIVE, and CORR-329 is why. 63.7 per cent of all IMPC knockouts are shorter and significant hits run 245 negative to 38 positive, so EVERY significant row here - Kdm5b -0.934, Kmt2d -2.005, Setd2 -3.898 - sits in the common direction and carries almost no information. The only row in the RARE direction is Kdm5a het +0.465 and it is not significant (P=0.250). The mouse cannot adjudicate this module.
why_it_matters: If LOXL2's height effect is nuclear rather than matrix it explains (a) why mcnerny2015's BAPN reduced BONE COLLAGEN cross-linking and left tibia length at p=0.580, (b) why the cartilage-specific Loxl2 knockout literature (Acan-Cre;Loxl2fl/fl, two labs) says LOXL2 PROTECTS cartilage while human genetics say losing it makes people taller - two different functions of one protein, and (c) why round 312's rat matrix-based contrast ran backwards.
compound_status: NO clinical-stage KDM5 inhibitor exists; the class (CPI-455, KDM5-C70) is preclinical and cancer-focused. PXS-5505 and BAPN inhibit the LOXL2 CATALYTIC amine oxidase site, which is the same site used for H3K4me3 deamination - so a LOX inhibitor should engage the nuclear function too, and whether it reaches the nuclear pool is unmeasured.
caution: Endothelial-specific KDM5A deficiency shortens lifespan and causes skeletal kyphosis (PMID 41236095).
